I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $549 cash and am on INDIANA_AVENUE. I own a light blue monopoly and several other unmortgaged properties. Building three houses on each light blue property costs $450, leaving me with $99.

Standard Monopoly rules require even building. I cannot place four houses on one property and three on another. Connecticut's rent at three houses is $300, while Oriental and Vermont are $270 each.

I am checking whether player three can land on my properties via a Chance card. They are currently on the Chance space, and I am reviewing the standard board layout to see which spaces they might reach.

I am reconsidering which Chance space player three landed on after passing GO. If they landed on the first Chance between Oriental and Vermont, a "Go Back 3 Spaces" card would send them to Income Tax rather than my properties.

Player three likely landed on the first Chance space after passing GO. A "Go Back 3 Spaces" card from there would send them to Income Tax rather than my properties. Other Chance cards do not specifically target Vermont or Connecticut.

I am reconsidering which Chance space player three landed on. The first Chance is at space 7, but a "Go Back 3 Spaces" card from there would send them to Income Tax rather than Oriental. I am now checking whether they might have landed on the second or third Chance instead.

Player three most likely landed on the first Chance space at position 7. A "Go Back 3 Spaces" card from there would send them to Income Tax rather than my properties. This earlier assumption was slightly wrong, but building houses remains the correct play because my light blue monopoly is my only major asset.

Player one owns a red monopoly with houses on Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois. Player two owns an orange set with houses on St. James, Tennessee, and New York. Player three owns dark blue properties with a Park Place of two houses and a Boardwalk of three, which are extremely dangerous. I need income to survive.

The $99 cash remaining after building covers the $90 rent for Indiana if I land there again. I will move next turn. Selling all nine houses back at half price would raise $225 in an emergency.

Mortgaging States, Ventnor, Pacific, and North Carolina would raise $500 in emergency funds. Combined with the $225 house sellback and remaining cash, total liquidity reaches $824. Player two's New York Avenue at three houses would cost $600 in rent.

Player one's red properties now cost $250 on Kentucky and $300 on Illinois. Player two's New York Avenue at three houses is $600. Player three's Boardwalk at three houses is $1400, which exceeds my total emergency liquidity of $824. Park Place at two houses is $500, which I can survive by liquidating assets.

I considered building only two houses on each property to preserve more cash, but that would leave the rent at $90 or $100. Three houses is the critical breakpoint that forces opponents to pay higher rent and potentially sell their own houses. The even-building rule requires all three properties to have exactly three houses.

I will build three houses on each light blue property now. I am skipping trades and additional mortgages to preserve cash for the house construction.

I will issue a confident public message and keep private notes honest. Nine light blue houses cost $450, leaving $99 cash, and the bank has enough stock. I will submit one build plan with all nine properties at once so the houses are ready before the turn ends.

Player one is on the B&O Railroad. They must roll around the board to reach my light blue properties. The houses will be ready before they land.

Player two is on Virginia and will not reach the light blues immediately. Player three is on the Chance space, so they will roll from there next turn. They could land on Vermont or Connecticut with a roll of one or two. I will move before them in the turn order.

Player three has zero cash. A roll of one or two onto Vermont or Connecticut would force them to sell dark blue houses to pay rent. Selling three houses would raise roughly $300, but it would also drop their Boardwalk rent from $1400 toward a lower level.
